reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to ~1200+/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), and 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are tied to ACTUAL metered reads rather than estimates (E-03), indicating a billing-calculation or rate-application defect in the billing import step is the dominant driver of the surge, not estimate substitution from field-read gaps or AMI export issues. This rules out a tariff change (E-02) and CRM response-time backlog (E-04) as causes, and contradicts the field-read-gap and AMI-export-failure mechanisms as the primary driver (both contradicted by E-03).
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to ~1220+/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). The dominant identified driver is billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which flags high consumption by comparing the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 usage history with no unit scaling (E-12); because firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report reads in a native register unit of "0.1 m3" rather than "m3" (E-13), BV-17 misflags their valid high-but-correct consumption as anomalous and rejects the read at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution. This pathway explains 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11); the cause of the larger segment of disputes tied to ACTUAL metered reads (1785 of 3025, E-03) is not yet established and is not assumed to share this mechanism.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
